title: Reading Comprehension - {La Première Page}
description: See how much you've mastered! Motion, possession, and complex pronouns in action.
can_do: Read complex French stories with advanced grammar
Understand movement, possession, and object pronouns in context

passage.speaker: Sophie
passage.fr: Bonjour Marc ! Tu viens au Café de la Paix avec moi ?
passage.en: Hello Marc! Are you coming to Café de la Paix with me?

passage.speaker: Marc
passage.fr: Oui ! Je vais au café avec toi. Tu as Le Comte de Monte-Cristo ? C'est le livre rouge et jaune.
passage.en: Yes! I'm going to the café with you. Do you have the Count of Monte Cristo? It's the red and yellow book.

img.alt: Sophie, in a long cream dress, meets Marc, in a brown suit, on a Paris boulevard; Marc holds up a red and yellow book.

passage.speaker: Sophie
passage.fr: Oui, je l'ai. Il est très vieux ! C'est le tien ?
passage.en: Yes, I have it. It's very old! Is it yours?

passage.speaker: Marc
passage.fr: Oui, c'est le mien. Tu le veux ?
passage.en: Yes, it's mine. Do you want it?

passage.speaker: Sophie
passage.fr: Non, merci ! J'ai mon livre de Jules Verne, Vingt mille lieues sous les mers. Il est nouveau. Tu veux le voir ?
passage.en: No, thank you! I have my Jules Verne book. Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea. It's new, do you want to see it?

img.alt: Sophie shows Marc her new dark-blue book with a small gold submarine on the cover, under a flowering chestnut tree by the Seine.

passage.speaker: Marc
passage.fr: Oui, s'il te plaît, au café.

passage.speaker: Sophie
passage.fr: Où est ton ami Paul ? Il vient aussi ?
passage.en: Where is your friend Paul? Is he coming too?

passage.speaker: Marc
passage.fr: Non, il part à Montmartre. Il a son jeune enfant aujourd'hui et il le voit à la maison.
passage.en: No, he's leaving for Montmartre. He has his young child today and he sees him at home.

passage.fr: Paul et son jeune enfant à Montmartre.
passage.en: Paul and his young child in Montmartre.

img.alt: Paul, in a grey coat and flat cap, walks hand in hand with his small son in a sailor suit up a Montmartre lane toward a windmill.

passage.speaker: Sophie
passage.fr: C'est bon. Tu as ses livres avec toi aussi ?
passage.en: That's good. Do you have his books with you also?

passage.speaker: Marc
passage.fr: Oui, ils sont dans ma voiture. Et j'ai un nouveau bon livre pour toi aussi !
passage.en: Yes, they're in my carriage (voiture). And I have a new good book for you too!

img.alt: Beside a horse-drawn carriage with books on the seat, Marc hands a new book to a smiling Sophie.

passage.speaker: Sophie
passage.fr: Oh ! Pour moi ? Merci ! Allons au café !
passage.en: Oh! For me? Thank you! Let's go to the café!

passage.speaker: Marc
passage.fr: Je veux un bon café avec toi.
passage.en: I want a good coffee with you.

passage.speaker: Sophie
passage.en: Yes! I want a good coffee with you!

passage.fr: Un bon café au Café de la Paix.
passage.en: A good coffee at the Café de la Paix.

img.alt: Sophie and Marc sit at a round marble table with two cups of coffee and a book inside the gilded Café de la Paix.

glossary.en: to the café, at the café

glossary.fr: Vingt mille lieues sous les mers
glossary.en: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea

items.question: Where does Sophie invite Marc?
items.hint: Look for {tu viens au ___} - what's the full café name?

mistakes.feedback: She invites him to the café, not the house
That's where Paul goes, not where Sophie invites Marc
café is masculine, use {au} not 'à la'

items.question: How does Marc respond to Sophie's invitation?
items.answer: Oui ! Je vais au café avec toi
accept: Je vais au café avec toi
items.hint: Marc's complete response to Sophie's invitation

mistakes.feedback: Marc accepts the invitation - he says {Oui! Je vais au café avec toi}
Marc agrees to go - he says {Oui! Je vais au café avec toi}

items.question: What book does Marc ask Sophie about?
items.hint: Look for the book title Marc mentions

mistakes.feedback: That's Sophie's book, not the one Marc asks about
That's Sophie's book, not the one Marc asks about

items.question: How does Sophie ask if the book belongs to Marc?

mistakes.feedback: Use possessive pronoun {le tien} not adjective 'ton'
Use possessive pronoun {le mien} not adjective 'mon'

items.question: Where does Paul go?
items.hint: Look for where Marc says Paul is going

mistakes.feedback: Paul doesn't come to the café, he goes to Montmartre
He goes to Montmartre first, then sees his child at home

items.question: Why can't Paul come to the café?
items.hint: Look for what Paul has today

mistakes.feedback: Paul has his young child, not a cat
Paul has his young child, not a book

items.question: What does Marc offer to give Sophie?
items.hint: Look for what Marc says he has for Sophie

mistakes.feedback: Marc offers a new (nouveau) book, not an old one
Marc offers a book (livre), not coffee

items.question: How does Sophie describe her book?
accept: un nouveau livre de Jules Verne
items.hint: Look for the adjective Sophie uses about her Jules Verne book

mistakes.feedback: Sophie's book is new (nouveau), Marc's book is old (vieux)
Sophie describes her book as new, not a color
a book is masculine, use {nouveau} not 'nouvelle'

items.question: How does Sophie describe Marc's book?
items.hint: Look for the adjective Sophie uses to describe the book

mistakes.feedback: Sophie says it's very old (vieux), not new
Book is masculine, use {vieux} not 'vielle'

items.question: Where does Marc say Paul's books are?
items.hint: Look for where Marc keeps the books

mistakes.feedback: The books are in the car (voiture), not at home
The books are in the car, not at the café

items.question: How does Sophie react when Marc offers her a book?
items.hint: Look for Sophie's surprised and grateful response to Marc's offer

mistakes.feedback: Sophie is excited and grateful, she says {Oh! Pour moi? Merci!}
Sophie accepts gratefully, she doesn't refuse the gift
